pr_title: [Subtitles] Improvements vertical margin and manual position
pr_body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->
in PR's where i have reworked subtitles renderer/features, i have introduced vertical margin support
(until now temporary can only be overwritten through advanced settings xml)
i have noticed that vertical margin can confuse some users (see #21298)

the reason is that the calibration window displays the value of the displayed text position
therefore implicitly exclude vertical margins (because the value is from top),
so the value saved in xml is the one with vertical margins.

to make it clearer the situation i have shown both values in Video calibration GUI:
![immagine](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3257156/165052014-8a8a19ec-ec5c-410a-8abe-45f8b93ea150.png)

and i have add a new GUI setting "vertical margin" (and removed the one in advanced settings):
![immagine](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3257156/165050527-4a6efc75-337c-4cf1-bbd7-e7c9b1506f6e.png)
in this way the user is aware of the vertical margin, and can read in the description that will influence also the Video calibration.

The value is in percentage instead of pixels, this to fit the screen resolution in use,
otherwise the value will results always wrong at the resolution change ("Adjust refresh rate" setting enabled case)

## Motivation and context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
An user #21298 think to a bug because did not understand the reason for the different value between xml file / GUI Calibration window

fix #21298 little bug in saving/loading position value
fix https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/21026#issuecomment-1104531231 to save value permanently position value changed via e.g. shortcut (kept after kodi restart)

## How has this been tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your change. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->

## What is the effect on users?
<!--- Summarize the effect of this change on Kodi end-users. -->
<!--- If the PR does not have a noticeable impact (e.g., if it only changes documentation), -->
<!--- just leave it empty. Put in more detail the bigger the impact is. -->
<!--- This section may be used for automatic creation of release notes. -->
better understand vertical margin functionality and its influence
allows to change vertical margin from GUI
can save permanently subtitle position changed e.g. via keyboard (by using e.g. `SubtitleShiftUp(save)`)

issue_context.title: Vertical subtitle position incorrectly written to / read from guisettings.xml
issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Since the 20220421 nightly (or maybe a bit sooner), the vertical subtitle position is incorrectly being written to / read from guisettings.xml.


## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Before the bug, I had the subtitle position for all my refresh rates set to 1008. When going back to the Video Calibration screen after configuring, this value was correctly shown again. And during playback, the subtitles were in the desired position.


## Actual Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
While playing some media, I noticed my subtitles were suddenly being displayed a lot higher vertically.
When I checked the Video Calibration screen, the value showed there as "933" even though it was previously set at 1008.
Even more strangely, when I set the value back to 1008 and then looked in guisettings.xml, the value stored there was 1083.
Also, when clearing out all resolutions from guisettings.xml and having Kodi write them fresh, the subtitle positions now defaults to the same value as the vertical resolution (i.e. 480 for all 720x480 resolutions, 720 for all 1280x720 resolutions and 1080 for all 1920x1080 resolutions; exception: 1080 is also set for all 3840x2160 resolutions).


## Possible Fix
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix or reason for the bug -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->



### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->
<!--- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
1. Go to System -> Video -> Video Calibration
2. Configure your desired subtitle position (I used 1008)
3. Exit the calibration screen
4. Exit Kodi
5. Check guisettings.xml. Value there shows as 1083
6. Restart Kodi and go to the calibration screen again. The subtitle position now shows 1005.


### Debuglog
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
<!--- A debuglog is always mandatory when creating an issue. Provide one! -->
The debuglog can be found here:
https://paste.kodi.tv/rinapiluxo.kodi


### Screenshots 
Here are some links or screenshots to help explain the problem:
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

<!--- Put your text below this line -->

Used Operating system:

comments:
Looking through the PRs I guess it has something to do with this one:

#21026

you have to consider the vertical margins that shift the text position,
then the position value shown in calibration GUI window, include the vertical margins,
this to make understand that the text is displayed in that pixel line

the default subtitle vertical margin is 75 pixel that can be overriden by adv settings, then:

1008 (base) + 75 default vertical margin = 1083 the real text displayed position

i will have to check better the behaviour in value saved
it is possible that I did not evaluate the saved value correctly

@CastagnaIT

Thanks for the explanation. I noticed that after closing Kodi and then going back to the calibration screen, the value for the subtitle position is shown as 1005 even though I saved it with 1008 (which shows as 1083 in guisettings.xml).

On the other hand, the subtitle position seems to be in the correct place once I saved it as 1008.

One other question: in your PR there is a screenshot showing an "after" picture where the first subtitle line is exactly inside the video and the second line is exactly in the black bar, which is exactly how I like it. Is this a new setting that can be configured so we don't have to mess with the vertical position manually anymore?

> the value for the subtitle position is shown as 1005 even though I saved it with 1008

yes this look weird and i would like to save the base value without the vertical margin, i will check this in the next days

> Is this a new setting that can be configured so we don't have to mess with the vertical position manually anymore?

i have only add more vertical margin, and yes for now can be customized from:
https://kodi.wiki/view/Advancedsettings.xml
search for `subtitleverticalmargin`

before the final version of Kodi 20 i would like to add it as a standard setting in the Kodi GUI settings and remove it from Advancedsettings.xml

@CastagnaIT Thanks for pointing me to this new setting.

For me the sweet spot for this value is 72.

This is with the subtitle position set to "Bottom of video", the Roboto Condensed font and a subtitle size of 48.

This gives me the first line of the subtitle just inside the video and the second line just in the black border.

PR #21313 is on the road when will be merged
you will able to change vertical margin from GUI settings (Advancedsettings removed)
the problem with load/save position value has been fixed
and Calibration setting window will show also the value with margins to make better understand the value difference
